summary: Walton Harbour Lighthouse, Minas Basin: a square wooden tower lit in 1872 or 1873 for the gypsum and barite port of Walton; a municipal museum since 1991, moved back from erosion in 2024.

light.characteristic: Fixed red (1872 to 1915); occulting white (1941 list)

structures.note: 6 m (20 ft) tower to the floor of the top deck, with an 8 ft lantern (NSLPS); Rowlett gives 8.5 m (28 ft) overall. Moved 45 m back in 2024.

access.note: Grounds open; tower open in season (daily early May to mid-October, donation requested).

facts.agency: Municipality of East Hants (owner); East Hants Tourism Association (maintains)

events.note: Light first put in operation 1 November 1872 (1874 Marine report, quoted by Lighthouse Friends). NSLPS gives 1873
Tower built by Timothy Parker, who was also first keeper; $520 contract; equipped cost $755.50 (1874 report) or $620 (NSLPS)
Timothy Parker appointed keeper in July 1873 (1874 report, quoted by Lighthouse Friends). LF keeper list starts 1872
Trees on the point cut down to give the light a larger range
Fourth-order Fresnel lens installed in the lantern; characteristic changed from fixed red to occulting white (Lighthouse Friends). NSLPS dates the 4th order dioptric lens to 1922
Automated (Lighthouse Friends). NSLPS says automated by 1986
Commercial shipping stopped after the barite mine closed; Rowlett: inactive since 1978
Department of Transport declared it surplus; Municipality of East Hants bought it for heritage
Designated heritage status on 12 August 1992 (NSLPS; Lighthouse Friends gives August 1992)
Craig Harding Award for Lighthouse Preservation (NSLPS)
Moved about 45 m (148 ft) back from the eroding bluff, November 2024 (Lighthouse Friends; Rowlett)

corrections.why: The record has no first-lit year. The 1874 Marine report, as quoted by Lighthouse Friends, says the light was put in operation on 1 November 1872.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett gives 1872 for the station. The 1874 Marine report, as quoted by Lighthouse Friends, says the light was put in operation on 1 November 1872 and that Parker was appointed keeper in July 1873. The NSLPS and the record give 1873 for the tower. The story gives 1872 for the light and 1873 for the tower and keeper.
Lighthouse Friends, quoting the 1874 report, gives a $520 contract and $755.50 for the equipped lighthouse. The NSLPS gives $620.00. The story gives both.
Lighthouse Friends dates the fourth-order Fresnel lens and the change to occulting white to 1915. The NSLPS history dates the 4th order dioptric lens and occulting white to 1922.
Lighthouse Friends gives automation in 1970 and extinguishing in 1986; the NSLPS gives automated by 1986; Rowlett gives inactive since 1978, the year shipping stopped. The story gives all three.

notes_for_editor: The 1874 Marine report is quoted only by Lighthouse Friends. The local corpus holds Marine reports for 1900 to 1924 only, so the 1872 and July 1873 dates are not checked against the original. The 1855 petition, the 1857 list and the 1860 renewal come from Lighthouse Friends alone; the House of Assembly journals were not read. The 1911 keeper table was checked in the page image on 2026-10-27 (archive.org/details/1912v46i14p21_0847, scan p. 246, printed p. 239): the Walton Harbour row reads Lewis E. Burgess, with an appointment date of 13 in 1903 (the month is a ditto of July on the row above), so the OCR 'K' was wrong and the row match is confirmed. The 1905 list ('Lewis E (Walton Harbour') agrees. The CBC article on the 2024 move did not load (timeout) and is not cited; the move is cited to Lighthouse Friends and Rowlett. Road names disagree: Lighthouse Friends says Pier Road off Route 215; Rowlett says Lorne Smith Road off NS 215; the story gives Route 215 only. Opening hours: Lighthouse Friends mid-May to mid-October; Rowlett early May to mid-October. The NSLPS names the East-Hants Tourism Association as maintainer and the Walton Area Development Association as operator. No wreck, storm or rescue at the light was found in the sources read, so that chapter is omitted. The NSLPS says 'the only surviving lighthouse in Hants County'; not used. Wikipedia, Scotia Sites and Waymarking were consulted for leads only and are not cited.
